_ C_ o_ m_ p_ u_ t_ e _ d_ e_ c_ o_ n_ v_ o_ l_ u_ t_ i_ o_ n

_ D_ e_ s_ c_ r_ i_ p_ t_ i_ o_ n:

     The function calculates cell abundance based on cell type
     signatures using different methods and signatures. Methods
     available are Quantiseq, CIBERSORTx, EpiDISH, DWLS and
     DeconRNASeq. Provided signatures included signatures based on bulk
     and methylation data. Signatures are present in the src/signatures
     directory, user can add its own signatures by adding the .txt
     files in this same folder. Second generation methods to perform
     deconvolution based on single cell data are also available if
     scRNAseq object is provided.

_ U_ s_ a_ g_ e:

     compute.deconvolution(
       raw.counts,
       methods = c("Quantiseq", "CBSX", "Epidish", "DeconRNASeq", "DWLS"),
       signatures_select = NULL,
       normalized = TRUE,
       doParallel = FALSE,
       workers = NULL,
       return = TRUE,
       create_signature = FALSE,
       credentials.mail = NULL,
       credentials.token = NULL,
       sc_deconv = FALSE,
       sc_matrix = NULL,
       sc_metadata = NULL,
       methods_sc = c("Autogenes", "BayesPrism", "Bisque", "CPM", "MuSic", "SCDC"),
       cell_label = NULL,
       sample_label = NULL,
       cell_markers = NULL,
       methods_sig = c("DWLS", "CIBERSORTx", "MOMF", "BSeqsc"),
       name_sc_signature = NULL,
       file_name = NULL,
       cells_extra = NULL
     )
     
_ A_ r_ g_ u_ m_ e_ n_ t_ s:

raw.counts: A matrix with the raw counts (samples as columns and genes
          symbols as rows)

 methods: A character vector with the deconvolution methods to run.
          Default are "Quantiseq", "CBSX", "Epidish", "DeconRNASeq",
          "DWLS"

signatures_select: A character vector with the signature names to run.
          If NULL (default), all available signatures are used (package
          signatures + custom signatures from
          Results/custom_signatures/).

normalized: If raw.counts are not available, user can input its
          normalized counts. In that case this argument need to be set
          to False.

doParallel: Whether to do or not parallelization. Only CBSX and DWLS
          methods will run in parallel.

 workers: Number of processes available to run on parallel. If no
          number is set, this will correspond to detectCores() - 1

  return: Whether to save or not the csv file with the deconvolution
          features

create_signature: Whether to create or not the signatures using the
          methods MOMF, CBSX, DWLS and BSeq-SC. If TRUE, sc_matrix
          shuld be provide.

credentials.mail: (Optional) Credential email for running CIBERSORTx.
          If not provided, CIBERSORTx method will not be run.

credentials.token: (Optional) Credential token for running CIBERSORTx.
          If not provided, CIBERSORTx method will not be run.

sc_deconv: Whether to run or not deconvolution methods based on single
          cell.

sc_matrix: If sc_deconv = T, the matrix of counts across cells from the
          scRNAseq object is provided.

sc_metadata: Dataframe with metadata from the single cell object. The
          matrix should include the columns cell_label and
          sample_label.

methods_sc: A character vector with the sc-deconvolution methods to
          run. Default are "Autogenes", "BayesPrism", "Bisque", "CPM",
          "MuSic", "SCDC"

cell_label: If sc_deconv = T, a character vector indicating the cell
          labels (same order as the count matrix)

sample_label: If sc_deconv = T, a character vector indicating the cell
          samples IDs (same order as the count matrix)

cell_markers: Named list with the genes markers names as Symbol per
          cell types to be used to create the signature using the
          BSeq-SC method. If NULL, the method will be ignored during
          the signature creation.

methods_sig: A character vector specifying which methods to run.
          Options are "DWLS", "CIBERSORTx", "MOMF", and "BSeqsc".
          Default runs all available methods.

name_sc_signature: If sc_deconv = T, the name you want to give to the
          signature generated

file_name: File name for the csv files and plots saved in the Results/
          directory

cells_extra: A character vector of non-standard cell type names to
          retain during analysis.

_ V_ a_ l_ u_ e:

     A matrix of cell type deconvolution features across samples

_ R_ e_ f_ e_ r_ e_ n_ c_ e_ s:

     Sturm, G., Finotello, F., Petitprez, F., Zhang, J. D., Baumbach,
     J., Fridman, W. H., ..., List, M., Aneichyk, T. (2019).
     Comprehensive evaluation of transcriptome-based cell-type
     quantification methods for immuno-oncology. Bioinformatics,
     35(14), i436-i445. https://doi.org/10.1093/bioinformatics/btz363

     Benchmarking second-generation methods for cell-type deconvolution
     of transcriptomic data. Dietrich, Alexander and Merotto, Lorenzo
     and Pelz, Konstantin and Eder, Bernhard and Zackl, Constantin and

_ D_ e_ s_ c_ r_ i_ p_ t_ i_ o_ n:

     The function calculates cell abundance based on cell type
     signatures using different methods and signatures. Methods
     available are Quantiseq, CIBERSORTx, EpiDISH, DWLS and
     DeconRNASeq. Provided signatures included signatures based on bulk
     and methylation data. Signatures are present in the src/signatures
     directory, user can add its own signatures by adding the .txt
     files in this same folder. Second generation methods to perform
     deconvolution based on single cell data are also available if
     scRNAseq object is provided.

       methods = c("Quantiseq", "CBSX", "Epidish", "DeconRNASeq", "DWLS"),
       signatures_select = NULL,
       normalized = TRUE,
       doParallel = FALSE,
       workers = NULL,
       return = TRUE,
       create_signature = FALSE,
       credentials.mail = NULL,
       credentials.token = NULL,
       sc_deconv = FALSE,

       sample_label = NULL,

          "DWLS"

signatures_select: A character vector with the signature names to run.
          If NULL (default), all available signatures are used (package
          signatures + custom signatures from
          Results/custom_signatures/).

normalized: If raw.counts are not available, user can input its
          normalized counts. In that case this argument need to be set
          to False.

doParallel: Whether to do or not parallelization. Only CBSX and DWLS
          methods will run in parallel.

          number is set, this will correspond to detectCores() - 1

          features

create_signature: Whether to create or not the signatures using the
          methods MOMF, CBSX, DWLS and BSeq-SC. If TRUE, sc_matrix
          shuld be provide.

credentials.mail: (Optional) Credential email for running CIBERSORTx.
          If not provided, CIBERSORTx method will not be run.

credentials.token: (Optional) Credential token for running CIBERSORTx.

          cell.

sc_matrix: If sc_deconv = T, the matrix of counts across cells from the
          scRNAseq object is provided.

methods_sc: A character vector with the sc-deconvolution methods to

     This function trains several machine learning models using
     repeated k-fold cross-validation, with hyperparameter tuning, and
     supports both classification and survival tasks. It allows
     flexible cross-validation schemes, including:

        • Standard stratified k-fold cross-validation

        • User-defined custom fold construction via a

       seed = 123,
       preprocess = TRUE
     )
     
_ A_ r_ g_ u_ m_ e_ n_ t_ s:

          columns.

task_type: Character. Prediction task type: ‘"classification"’ or
          ‘"survival"’.

target_var: Vector. Target variable for classification tasks: one value
          per sample, in the same order as the rows of
          ‘features_train’, without missing values.

trait.positive: Value in ‘target_var’ representing the positive class.
          All other values form the negative class.

time_var: Numeric vector. Survival/follow-up time of each sample, in
          the same order as the rows of ‘features_train’ (required for
          survival tasks).

event_var: Vector. Event indicator of each sample (1 = event occurred,
          0 = censored), in the same order as the rows of
          ‘features_train’ (required for survival tasks).

  metric: Character. Performance metric for model selection and tuning
          (classification):

            • ‘"AUROC"’ - area under the ROC curve (used when ‘NULL’)

            • ‘"AUPRC"’ - area under the precision-recall curve

          Survival models are always selected by the concordance index
          (C-index); ‘metric’ is ignored.

 k_folds: Integer. Number of folds for cross-validation. Default: 10.

   n_rep: Integer. Number of repetitions for repeated CV. Default: 5.

    LODO: Logical. If ‘TRUE’, the cross-validation folds are stratified
          by cohort and outcome, for Leave-One-Dataset-Out analyses
          (train on some cohorts, test on a left-out one). The cohort
          is not used as a predictor.

batch_var: Vector. Cohort/batch of each sample, in the same order as
          the rows of ‘features_train’. Required if ‘LODO = TRUE’. For
          classification, each cohort needs at least ‘k_folds’ samples.

file_name: Character. File name prefix used to save performance plots
          in ‘"Results/"’.

          (cross-validation folds are processed in parallel). Default:
          ‘NULL’ (sequential). For classification with
          ‘fold_construction_fun’, the models are trained sequentially
          and ‘ncores’ is not used.

  return: Logical. Whether to save the cross-validation performance
          plots in ‘"Results/"’. Default: ‘FALSE’.

fold_construction_fun: Function. Optional user-defined function for
          fold construction. It is called with ‘data’ (the training
          features plus the outcome: a ‘target’ column coded
          ‘"no"’/‘"yes"’ for classification, ‘time’ and ‘event’ columns
          for survival), ‘folds’ and ‘bestune’. It must remove the
          outcome columns before building features. Must accept a
          ‘bestune’ argument:

            • ‘bestune = NULL’ - build the features of every fold (for
              every combination of the tunable arguments, if any) and
              save them. The function can run its own parallel workers
              for this.

            • ‘bestune provided’ - rebuild features on the full dataset
              using optimized parameters, and return a list with the
              features plus the outcome columns, any custom output, and
              ‘bestune’ (with tunable arguments: a data frame with the
              selected values of these arguments).

     The function supports both classification and survival analysis
     pipelines via ‘task_type = "classification"’ or ‘task_type =
     "survival"’.

     Classification trains and tunes 11 algorithms with ‘caret’
     (‘treebag’, ‘rf’, ‘C5.0’, ‘glmnet’, lasso, ridge, ‘knn’, ‘rpart’,
     ‘svmRadial’, ‘svmLinear’, ‘xgbTree’). Survival trains and tunes 6
     models with ‘parsnip’ and ‘censored’ (Cox PH, elastic-net Cox,
     parametric AFT, conditional inference tree, bagged CART, oblique
     random survival forest). The best model is selected by the
     cross-validation ‘metric’ (classification) or C-index (survival),
     and trained on all training samples with its tuned
     hyperparameters.

     pair of features with an absolute correlation above 0.9, one of
     the two are removed. The outcome is not used. Without
     ‘fold_construction_fun’, this is done once on all training samples
     before the cross-validation, so the folds and the final model use
     the same features. The test samples are not involved:
     ‘compute_prediction()’ keeps the features of the final model.

     fold are built by that function, and the preprocessing is done
     inside each fold: on the features built on the training part,
     keeping the same features in the held-out part. The final model is
     trained on the features the function builds on all training
     samples, preprocessed in the same way. See

     Applies a trained model to a test set and evaluates it. For
     classification, it computes AUROC and AUPRC with bootstrap
     confidence intervals, and Accuracy, Sensitivity, Specificity,
     Precision, Recall, F1 score and MCC at each probability threshold.
     For survival, it predicts risk scores and computes the C-index.

     compute_prediction(
       model,
       test_data,
       target_var = NULL,
       trait.positive = NULL,
       task_type = "classification",
       time_var = NULL,
       event_var = NULL,
       file.name = NULL,

     )
     
_ A_ r_ g_ u_ m_ e_ n_ t_ s:

   model: The trained model returned as ‘$Model’ by
          ‘compute_features.training.ML()’ (e.g. ‘res$Model’).

test_data: A data frame of predictor variables for the test set (for
          classification, a matrix is also accepted). It must contain
          all the features of the model; other columns are ignored for
          classification.

target_var: Vector of true labels for the test set, in the order of the
          rows of ‘test_data’ (classification only).

trait.positive: Value in ‘target_var’ representing the positive class
          (classification only).

task_type: Character. Either ‘"classification"’ or ‘"survival"’.

time_var: Numeric vector of survival/follow-up times of the test
          samples, in the order of the rows of ‘test_data’ (required
          for survival tasks).

event_var: Numeric vector of event indicators of the test samples (1 =
          event, 0 = censored; required for survival tasks).

file.name: Character. File name prefix of the plots saved in
          ‘Results/’.

  return: Logical. Whether to save the plots in ‘Results/’ (ROC and
          precision-recall curves for classification, Kaplan-Meier
          curves by predicted risk group for survival). Default =
          FALSE.

n_groups: Integer. Number of risk groups of the Kaplan-Meier plot
          (survival only, used with ‘return = TRUE’). Default = 2. See
          ‘plot_survival_performance()’.

_ D_ e_ t_ a_ i_ l_ s:

     Confidence intervals of AUROC and AUPRC come from 1000 bootstrap
     resamples of the test samples, stratified by class (positives and
     negatives resampled separately, so every resample has both), and
     the confidence interval of the C-index from 1000 bootstrap
     resamples stratified by event. Both use the fixed seed 123 only
     inside the bootstrap: the state of the random number generator of
     the session is not changed.

     Survival models can predict a linear predictor, a survival time or
     a survival probability. The modelling library returns all three so
     that higher values mean longer survival (also the linear predictor
     of Cox models); they are reversed, so that higher predictions
     always mean higher risk.

_ V_ a_ l_ u_ e:

     For classification, a list containing:

     ‘Metrics’ Data frame of performance metrics (Accuracy,
          Sensitivity, Specificity, Precision, Recall, F1 score, MCC)
          for each threshold: one row per test sample, sorted by
          decreasing predicted probability.

     ‘AUC’ List with ‘AUROC’ and ‘AUPRC’, each a list with the
          ‘estimate’ on the test set and the ‘lower’ and ‘upper’ bounds
          of its 95% bootstrap confidence interval.

     ‘Predictions’ Data frame of predicted probabilities for each class
          (columns ‘no’ and ‘yes’), in the order of the rows of
          ‘test_data’.

     ‘Curve_bands’ List with ‘ROC’ (columns ‘fpr’, ‘lower’, ‘upper’)
          and ‘PRC’ (columns ‘recall’, ‘lower’, ‘upper’): pointwise 95%
          bootstrap bands around the ROC and precision-recall curves.

     ‘preds’ Predicted risk scores (higher values mean higher risk).

_ D_ e_ s_ c_ r_ i_ p_ t_ i_ o_ n:

     This function calculates SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations)
     values to assess feature importance for the final model selected
     by ‘compute_features.training.ML()’, i.e. the model trained on all
     training samples with the tuned hyperparameters. SHAP values are
     computed for every training sample, on the features of the final
     model, so each feature has the same definition for all samples
     (including features built by a custom fold construction function,
     which are computed once on all training samples). It supports both
     classification and survival tasks.

_ U_ s_ a_ g_ e:

     compute_shap_values(model_trained, task_type = "classification", seed = 123)
     
_ A_ r_ g_ u_ m_ e_ n_ t_ s:

model_trained: The trained model returned as ‘$Model’ by
          ‘compute_features.training.ML()’ (e.g. ‘res$Model’).
          Everything else is taken from it:

            • Classification: the caret ‘train’ object; features of the
              training samples from ‘$trainingData’; SHAP values
              explain the predicted probability of the positive class
              (‘"yes"’).

            • Survival: the final fitted model in ‘$Model_object’;
              features of the training samples from ‘$trainingData’
              (the ‘time’ and ‘event’ columns are not used as
              features); SHAP values explain the predicted risk score.

task_type: Character. Either ‘"classification"’ (default) or
          ‘"survival"’.

    seed: Integer. Random seed for reproducible SHAP values (they are
          Monte Carlo estimates). Default: ‘123’. Use ‘NULL’ to leave
          the random number generator untouched.

_ D_ e_ t_ a_ i_ l_ s:

     SHAP values are estimated with ‘fastshap::explain()’ (100 Monte
     Carlo simulations per feature), using the training samples both as
     the samples to explain and as background data.

     Because the final model was trained on the samples it explains,
     SHAP values describe how the model uses each feature on its
     training data. With flexible models and small datasets, a model
     that overfits can assign importance to features that help fit the
     training samples but do not generalize: compare the training
     performance with the cross-validation performance before
     interpreting them.

_ V_ a_ l_ u_ e:

     A data frame of SHAP values, with rows corresponding to training
     samples (sample IDs as rownames) and columns to the features of
     the final model. Values are in the units of the model output
     (probability of the positive class for classification, risk score
     for survival). The average prediction of the model on the training
     samples is stored in the attribute ‘"baseline"’: for each sample,
     the baseline plus the sum of its SHAP values equals its
     prediction. If the model predicts the same value for all samples,
     a warning is issued and ‘NULL’ is returned.

_ E_ x_ a_ m_ p_ l_ e_ s:

     ## Not run:

                                         target_var = data_example_classification$target,
                                         task_type = "classification",
                                         trait.positive = "1",
                                         k_folds = 5,
                                         n_rep = 2)
     
     shap <- compute_shap_values(res$Model, task_type = "classification")
     head(shap)
     
     # Global importance: mean absolute SHAP value of each feature
     sort(colMeans(abs(shap)), decreasing = TRUE)
     ## End(Not run)

_ D_ e_ s_ c_ r_ i_ p_ t_ i_ o_ n:

     This function calculates SHAP (SHapley Additive exPlanations)
     values to assess feature importance for the final model selected
     by ‘compute_features.training.ML()’, i.e. the model trained on all
     training samples with the tuned hyperparameters. SHAP values are
     computed for every training sample, on the features of the final
     model, so each feature has the same definition for all samples
     (including features built by a custom fold construction function,
     which are computed once on all training samples). It supports both
     classification and survival tasks.

_ U_ s_ a_ g_ e:

     compute_shap_values(model_trained, task_type = "classification", seed = 123)
     
_ A_ r_ g_ u_ m_ e_ n_ t_ s:

model_trained: The trained model returned as ‘$Model’ by
          ‘compute_features.training.ML()’ (e.g. ‘res$Model’).
          Everything else is taken from it:

            • Classification: the caret ‘train’ object; features of the
              training samples from ‘$trainingData’; SHAP values
              explain the predicted probability of the positive class
              (‘"yes"’).

            • Survival: the final fitted model in ‘$Model_object’;
              features of the training samples from ‘$trainingData’
              (the ‘time’ and ‘event’ columns are not used as
              features); SHAP values explain the predicted risk score.

task_type: Character. Either ‘"classification"’ (default) or
          ‘"survival"’.

    seed: Integer. Random seed for reproducible SHAP values (they are
          Monte Carlo estimates). Default: ‘123’. Use ‘NULL’ to leave
          the random number generator untouched.

_ D_ e_ t_ a_ i_ l_ s:

     SHAP values are estimated with ‘fastshap::explain()’ (100 Monte
     Carlo simulations per feature), using the training samples both as
     the samples to explain and as background data.

     Because the final model was trained on the samples it explains,
     SHAP values describe how the model uses each feature on its
     training data. With flexible models and small datasets, a model
     that overfits can assign importance to features that help fit the
     training samples but do not generalize: compare the training
     performance with the cross-validation performance before
     interpreting them.

_ V_ a_ l_ u_ e:

     A data frame of SHAP values, with rows corresponding to training
     samples (sample IDs as rownames) and columns to the features of
     the final model. Values are in the units of the model output
     (probability of the positive class for classification, risk score
     for survival). The average prediction of the model on the training
     samples is stored in the attribute ‘"baseline"’: for each sample,
     the baseline plus the sum of its SHAP values equals its
     prediction. If the model predicts the same value for all samples,
     a warning is issued and ‘NULL’ is returned.

prepare_multideconv_folds <- function(
    data,
    folds = NULL,
    bestune = NULL,
    ncores = NULL,
    cells_extra = NULL,
    corr = 0.7,
    corr_type = "spearman",
    zero_thr = 0.9,
    cv_thr = 0.1,
    batch = NULL
) {

  # Outcome columns given by pipeML in data: "target" (classification) or "time" + "event" (survival).
  # They are removed before computing the deconvolution subgroups and added back to the returned data
  if ("target" %in% colnames(data)) {
    outcome_cols <- "target"
  } else if (all(c("time", "event") %in% colnames(data))) {
    outcome_cols <- c("time", "event")
  } else {
    stop("data must contain a 'target' column (classification) or 'time' and 'event' columns (survival)")
  }
  survival <- !identical(outcome_cols, "target")
  outcome <- data[, outcome_cols, drop = FALSE]
  data <- data[, setdiff(colnames(data), outcome_cols), drop = FALSE]

  # -----------------------------
  # CASE 1: bestune provided - compute full training once
  # -----------------------------
  if (!is.null(bestune)) {

    # Compute deconvolution on full dataset
    deconv_subgroups_final <- compute.deconvolution.analysis(
      deconvolution = data,
      corr = corr,
      corr_type = corr_type,
      zero_thr = zero_thr,
      cv_thr = cv_thr,
      batch = batch,
      cells_extra = cells_extra,
      return = FALSE,
      verbose = FALSE
    )

    train_cell_data_final <- cbind(deconv_subgroups_final[[1]], outcome)

    custom_output <- deconv_subgroups_final

    return(list(train_cell_data_final, custom_output, bestune))
  }

  # -----------------------------
  # CASE 2: bestune NOT provided - compute folds
  # -----------------------------
  if (is.null(folds)) stop("Provide 'folds' (a list of training row indices) or 'bestune'.")
  if (is.null(ncores)) ncores <- max(1, parallel::detectCores() - 2)
  cl <- parallel::makeCluster(ncores)
  doParallel::registerDoParallel(cl)

  processed_folds <- foreach::foreach(
    i = seq_along(folds),
    .packages = c("dplyr", "multideconv")
  ) %dopar% {
    cat("Starting fold", names(folds)[i], "\n")

    train_idx <- folds[[i]]
    test_idx  <- setdiff(seq_len(nrow(data)), train_idx)

    # TRAIN: subgroups learned on the training samples of the fold
    deconv_subgroups <- compute.deconvolution.analysis(
      deconvolution = data[train_idx, , drop = FALSE],
      corr = corr,
      corr_type = corr_type,
      zero_thr = zero_thr,
      cv_thr = cv_thr,
      batch = if (!is.null(batch)) batch[train_idx] else NULL,
      cells_extra = cells_extra,
      return = FALSE
    )

    train_cell_data <- cbind(deconv_subgroups[[1]], outcome[train_idx, , drop = FALSE])

    # TEST: test samples projected onto the subgroups learned on the training samples
    test_data <- replicate_deconvolution_subgroups(deconv_subgroups, data[test_idx, , drop = FALSE])
    if (survival) test_data <- cbind(test_data, outcome[test_idx, , drop = FALSE])  # pipeML evaluates each fold with them

    list(
      train_data = train_cell_data,
      test_data  = test_data,
      obs_test   = if (survival) outcome[test_idx, , drop = FALSE] else outcome$target[test_idx],
      rowIndex   = test_idx,
      fold_name  = names(folds)[i]
    )
  }

  parallel::stopCluster(cl)
  unregister_dopar()

  # Save each fold (pipeML reads back every Results/fold_*.rds, so drop stale files from earlier runs first)
  ensure_results_dir()
  file.remove(list.files("Results", pattern = "^fold_.*\\.rds$", full.names = TRUE))
  fold_names <- if (is.null(names(folds))) paste0("Fold", seq_along(folds)) else names(folds)
  names(processed_folds) <- fold_names
  for (i in seq_along(processed_folds)) {
    saveRDS(processed_folds[[i]], file = file.path("Results", paste0("fold_", fold_names[i], ".rds")))
  }

  invisible(processed_folds)
}

#' Relate Deconvolution Subgroups to Pathway Activities
#'
#' Correlates deconvolution subgroup profiles with a pre-computed pathway
#' activity matrix, saves one heatmap per cell type to `Results/` and returns
#' the correlations and p-values.
#'
#' @param subgroups Output list from [compute.deconvolution.analysis()].
#' @param pathways A numeric matrix or data frame with samples as rows and
#'   pathway activities as columns. Row names must match sample identifiers in
#'   `subgroups`.
#' @param file_name Character prefix used when naming output PDF files.
#' @param height,width Plot height and width in inches (passed to [ggplot2::ggsave()]). If `NULL` (default), the
#'   size is chosen from the number of subgroups and pathways.
#' @param par_mar Ignored; kept for backwards compatibility.
#' @param pval P-value threshold; correlations above this are not starred.
#' @param corr_type Correlation type, "pearson" (default) or "spearman".
#'
#' @return Invisibly, a list with one element per cell type, each holding `correlations` and `pvalues`
#'   (subgroups as rows, pathways as columns). One PDF heatmap per cell type is also saved in `Results/`.
#'
#' @importFrom ggplot2 ggplot aes geom_tile geom_text scale_fill_gradientn
#'   scale_x_discrete guide_colorbar labs theme_minimal theme element_text
#'   element_blank margin ggsave
#' @importFrom stats quantile
#' @export
compute.subgroup.pathways <- function(subgroups,
                                      pathways  = NULL,
                                      file_name = "Test",
                                      height    = NULL,

  #Remove models with same predictions across samples (not able to make distinction)
  model_predictions <- lapply(model_predictions, function(df) {
    df = df %>%
      dplyr::select(dplyr::where(~ dplyr::n_distinct(.) > 1))

    if(ncol(df) == 0){
      df = NULL
    }

    return(df)
  })

  model_predictions = Filter(Negate(is.null), model_predictions) #Discard not useful predictions
  ensembleResults = ensembleResults[names(model_predictions)] #Discard not useful models based on predictions

  if (length(ensembleResults) == 0) {
    stop("No model can be selected: every model predicts the same value for all training samples. ",
         "The features may not be informative for the outcome.\n")
  }

  #Clean memory
  rm(fit.treebag, fit.rf, fit.c50, fit.knn, fit.cart, fit.glmnet, fit.lasso, fit.ridge, fit.svm_radial, fit.svm_linear)
  gc()

  #Top model with best accuracy or AUC
  metrics = compute_cv_AUC(ensembleResults, file_name = file_name, AUC_type = metric, return = return)

  top_model = metrics[["Top_model"]]
  AUROC_median = metrics[["AUROC"]]
  AUPRC_median = metrics[["AUPRC"]]

  model = ensembleResults[[top_model]]

  cat("Best ML model found: ", top_model, "\n")

  cat("Returning model trained\n")

  output = list("Model" = model, "ML_Models" = ensembleResults, "AUROC_median" = AUROC_median, "AUPRC_median" = AUPRC_median)

  if(!is.null(custom_outputs) && !is.null(custom_outputs[[top_model]])){ # custom output of the selected model (other models may have been excluded)
    output[[length(output)+1]] = custom_outputs[[top_model]]
    names(output)[length(output)] = "Custom_output"
  }

  return(output)

## TME composition -> immunotherapy response prediction
## Train on Gide et al. cohort, validate on Riaz et al. cohort (independent cohorts)
## Pipeline: multideconv (cell-type deconvolution + leakage-free subgroup folds) + pipeML (ML training/prediction/SHAP)

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(multideconv)
  library(pipeML)
  library(dplyr)
})

work_dir    <- "/home/marcelo.hurtado/Documents/tme_analysis/d91d50f6b3/work"
data_dir    <- file.path(work_dir, "data")
results_dir <- file.path(work_dir, "results")

setwd(results_dir)  # package functions write to "Results/" relative to the working directory

set.seed(123)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Load data
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

coldata <- read.table(file.path(data_dir, "colData_all.txt"), header = TRUE, sep = " ", quote = "\"")
rownames(coldata) <- coldata$rna_id

gide <- read.delim(file.path(data_dir, "Gide_log2TPM.txt"), check.names = FALSE, row.names = 1)
riaz <- read.delim(file.path(data_dir, "Riaz_log2TPM.txt"), check.names = FALSE, row.names = 1)

# Values are log2(TPM + 1); multideconv expects linear-scale (TPM) counts
gide_tpm <- 2^gide - 1
riaz_tpm <- 2^riaz - 1
gide_tpm[gide_tpm < 0] <- 0
riaz_tpm[riaz_tpm < 0] <- 0

coldata_gide <- coldata[coldata$Cohort == "Gide", ]
coldata_riaz <- coldata[coldata$Cohort == "Riaz", ]

coldata_gide <- coldata_gide[colnames(gide_tpm), ]
coldata_riaz <- coldata_riaz[colnames(riaz_tpm), ]

stopifnot(all(rownames(coldata_gide) == colnames(gide_tpm)))
stopifnot(all(rownames(coldata_riaz) == colnames(riaz_tpm)))

cat("Gide (training cohort): ", ncol(gide_tpm), " samples - Response: ", paste(names(table(coldata_gide$Response)), table(coldata_gide$Response), sep = "=", collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Riaz (test cohort): ", ncol(riaz_tpm), " samples - Response: ", paste(names(table(coldata_riaz$Response)), table(coldata_riaz$Response), sep = "=", collapse = ", "), "\n")

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Cell type deconvolution (first-generation methods, multideconv)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

deconv_methods <- c("Quantiseq", "Epidish", "DeconRNASeq", "DWLS")

deconv_train <- multideconv::compute.deconvolution(
  raw.counts  = gide_tpm,
  methods     = deconv_methods,
  normalized  = FALSE,   # input is already TPM-normalized (not raw counts)
  doParallel  = TRUE,
  workers     = 4,
  return      = TRUE,
  file_name   = "Gide"
)

deconv_test <- multideconv::compute.deconvolution(
  raw.counts  = riaz_tpm,
  methods     = deconv_methods,
  normalized  = FALSE,
  doParallel  = TRUE,
  workers     = 4,
  return      = TRUE,
  file_name   = "Riaz"
)

# Keep clinical data in the same sample order as the deconvolution tables
traitData_train <- coldata_gide[rownames(deconv_train), , drop = FALSE]
traitData_test  <- coldata_riaz[rownames(deconv_test), , drop = FALSE]

saveRDS(list(deconv_train = deconv_train, deconv_test = deconv_test,
             traitData_train = traitData_train, traitData_test = traitData_test),
        file.path(results_dir, "deconvolution_tables.rds"))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Train classification model with leakage-free cross-validation
##    (deconvolution subgroups rebuilt inside every CV fold, via multideconv::prepare_multideconv_folds)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

res <- pipeML::compute_features.training.ML(
  features_train = deconv_train,
  target_var      = traitData_train$Response,
  task_type        = "classification",
  trait.positive   = "R",
  metric           = "AUROC",
  k_folds          = 5,
  n_rep            = 10,
  ncores           = NULL,
  return           = TRUE,
  file_name        = "Gide_training",
  fold_construction_fun       = multideconv::prepare_multideconv_folds,
  fold_construction_args_fixed = list(ncores = 4)
)

saveRDS(res, file.path(results_dir, "training_result.rds"))

cat("\n==== Cross-validation performance (Gide, training cohort) ====\n")
print(res$AUROC_median)
print(res$AUPRC_median)
cat("\nSelected model: ", res$Model$method, "\n")

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Predict on the independent Riaz cohort
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Project Riaz samples onto the deconvolution subgroups learned on Gide only
dt_test <- multideconv::replicate_deconvolution_subgroups(
  deconv_res         = res$Custom_output,
  deconvolution_test = deconv_test
)

pred <- pipeML::compute_prediction(
  model       = res$Model,
  test_data   = dt_test,
  target_var  = traitData_test$Response,
  task_type   = "classification",
  trait.positive = "R",
  file.name   = "Gide_to_Riaz",
  return      = TRUE
)

saveRDS(pred, file.path(results_dir, "test_prediction.rds"))

cat("\n==== Performance on the independent Riaz cohort ====\n")
print(pred$AUC)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. SHAP values: which TME subgroups drive the prediction?
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

shap <- pipeML::compute_shap_values(
  model_trained = res$Model,
  task_type     = "classification",
  seed          = 123
)

saveRDS(shap, file.path(results_dir, "shap_values.rds"))

importance <- sort(colMeans(abs(shap)), decreasing = TRUE)
importance_df <- data.frame(Feature = names(importance), Mean_abs_SHAP = unname(importance))
write.csv(importance_df, file.path(results_dir, "shap_feature_importance.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

cat("\n==== Top features driving the prediction (mean |SHAP|) ====\n")
print(head(importance_df, 15))

# Composition of the top subgroups (which method-signature-cell type estimates were merged)
subgroup_composition <- res$Custom_output[["Deconvolution subgroups composition"]]
top_features <- head(importance_df$Feature, 10)
composition_txt <- file.path(results_dir, "top_feature_composition.txt")
sink(composition_txt)
for (feat in top_features) {
  cell_type <- NULL
  for (ct in names(subgroup_composition)) {
    if (feat %in% names(subgroup_composition[[ct]])) {
      cell_type <- ct
      break
    }
  }
  cat("Feature: ", feat, "\n", sep = "")
  if (!is.null(cell_type)) {
    cat("  Cell type: ", cell_type, "\n", sep = "")
    cat("  Composed of (method_signature estimates merged into this subgroup):\n")
    cat("   - ", paste(subgroup_composition[[cell_type]][[feat]], collapse = "\n   - "), "\n\n", sep = "")
  } else {
    cat("  (single feature, not part of a merged subgroup)\n\n")
  }
}
sink()

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 6. SHAP plots
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(shapviz))

X_shap <- res$Model$trainingData[rownames(shap), colnames(shap)]
sv <- shapviz::shapviz(as.matrix(shap), X = X_shap, baseline = attr(shap, "baseline"))

pdf(file.path(results_dir, "SHAP_importance_bar.pdf"), width = 7, height = 6)
print(shapviz::sv_importance(sv, kind = "bar") + ggplot2::ggtitle("Global feature importance (mean |SHAP|)"))
dev.off()

pdf(file.path(results_dir, "SHAP_beeswarm.pdf"), width = 7, height = 6)
print(shapviz::sv_importance(sv, kind = "beeswarm") + ggplot2::ggtitle("SHAP values across training samples"))
dev.off()

top_feature <- importance_df$Feature[1]
pdf(file.path(results_dir, "SHAP_dependence_top_feature.pdf"), width = 6, height = 5)
print(shapviz::sv_dependence(sv, v = top_feature))
dev.off()

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 7. Written summary
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

summary_txt <- file.path(results_dir, "RESULTS_SUMMARY.txt")
sink(summary_txt)
cat("TME composition -> immunotherapy response prediction\n")
cat("======================================================\n\n")
cat("Training cohort: Gide et al. (n = ", ncol(gide_tpm), "; R = ", sum(traitData_train$Response == "R"),
    ", NR = ", sum(traitData_train$Response == "NR"), ")\n", sep = "")
cat("Test cohort:     Riaz et al. (n = ", ncol(riaz_tpm), "; R = ", sum(traitData_test$Response == "R"),
    ", NR = ", sum(traitData_test$Response == "NR"), ")\n\n", sep = "")

cat("Deconvolution methods: ", paste(deconv_methods, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Number of raw deconvolution features (Gide): ", ncol(deconv_train), "\n")
cat("Number of deconvolution subgroup features used by the final model: ", ncol(res$Model$trainingData) - 1, "\n\n")

cat("Selected ML algorithm: ", res$Model$method, "\n")
cat("Best hyperparameters:\n")
print(res$Model$bestTune)

cat("\nCross-validation performance on Gide (median [MAD] across resamples):\n")
print(res$AUROC_median)
print(res$AUPRC_median)

cat("\nIndependent validation on Riaz:\n")
cat("  AUROC = ", round(pred$AUC$AUROC$estimate, 3),
    " [", round(pred$AUC$AUROC$lower, 3), "-", round(pred$AUC$AUROC$upper, 3), "]\n", sep = "")
cat("  AUPRC = ", round(pred$AUC$AUPRC$estimate, 3),
    " [", round(pred$AUC$AUPRC$lower, 3), "-", round(pred$AUC$AUPRC$upper, 3), "]\n", sep = "")

cat("\nTop features driving the prediction (mean |SHAP| on the training data):\n")
print(head(importance_df, 15))
sink()

cat("\n\nDone. Results saved in: ", results_dir, "\n")

  model_trained = res$Model,

  cell_type <- NULL

    if (feat %in% names(subgroup_composition[[ct]])) {
      cell_type <- ct

    }
  }
  cat("Feature: ", feat, "\n", sep = "")
  if (!is.null(cell_type)) {
    cat("  Cell type: ", cell_type, "\n", sep = "")
    cat("  Composed of (method_signature estimates merged into this subgroup):\n")
    cat("   - ", paste(subgroup_composition[[cell_type]][[feat]], collapse = "\n   - "), "\n\n", sep = "")
  } else {
    cat("  (single feature, not part of a merged subgroup)\n\n")
  }
}
sink()

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

print(shapviz::sv_importance(sv, kind = "beeswarm") + ggplot2::ggtitle("SHAP values across training samples"))
dev.off()

dev.off()

## 7. Written summary
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

sink(summary_txt)

cat("======================================================\n\n")
cat("Training cohort: Gide et al. (n = ", ncol(gide_tpm), "; R = ", sum(traitData_train$Response == "R"),

## TME composition -> immunotherapy response prediction
## Train on Gide et al. cohort, validate on Riaz et al. cohort (independent cohorts)
## Pipeline: multideconv (cell-type deconvolution + leakage-free subgroup folds) + pipeML (ML training/prediction/SHAP)

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(multideconv)
  library(pipeML)
  library(dplyr)
})

work_dir    <- "/home/marcelo.hurtado/Documents/tme_analysis/d91d50f6b3/work"
data_dir    <- file.path(work_dir, "data")
results_dir <- file.path(work_dir, "results")

setwd(results_dir)  # package functions write to "Results/" relative to the working directory

set.seed(123)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Load data
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

coldata <- read.table(file.path(data_dir, "colData_all.txt"), header = TRUE, sep = " ", quote = "\"")
rownames(coldata) <- coldata$rna_id

gide <- read.delim(file.path(data_dir, "Gide_log2TPM.txt"), check.names = FALSE, row.names = 1)
riaz <- read.delim(file.path(data_dir, "Riaz_log2TPM.txt"), check.names = FALSE, row.names = 1)

# Values are log2(TPM + 1); multideconv expects linear-scale (TPM) counts
gide_tpm <- 2^gide - 1
riaz_tpm <- 2^riaz - 1
gide_tpm[gide_tpm < 0] <- 0
riaz_tpm[riaz_tpm < 0] <- 0

coldata_gide <- coldata[coldata$Cohort == "Gide", ]
coldata_riaz <- coldata[coldata$Cohort == "Riaz", ]

coldata_gide <- coldata_gide[colnames(gide_tpm), ]
coldata_riaz <- coldata_riaz[colnames(riaz_tpm), ]

stopifnot(all(rownames(coldata_gide) == colnames(gide_tpm)))
stopifnot(all(rownames(coldata_riaz) == colnames(riaz_tpm)))

cat("Gide (training cohort): ", ncol(gide_tpm), " samples - Response: ", paste(names(table(coldata_gide$Response)), table(coldata_gide$Response), sep = "=", collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Riaz (test cohort): ", ncol(riaz_tpm), " samples - Response: ", paste(names(table(coldata_riaz$Response)), table(coldata_riaz$Response), sep = "=", collapse = ", "), "\n")

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Cell type deconvolution (first-generation methods, multideconv)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

deconv_methods <- c("Quantiseq", "Epidish", "DeconRNASeq", "DWLS")

deconv_train <- multideconv::compute.deconvolution(
  raw.counts  = gide_tpm,
  methods     = deconv_methods,
  normalized  = FALSE,   # input is already TPM-normalized (not raw counts)
  doParallel  = TRUE,
  workers     = 4,
  return      = TRUE,
  file_name   = "Gide"
)

deconv_test <- multideconv::compute.deconvolution(
  raw.counts  = riaz_tpm,
  methods     = deconv_methods,
  normalized  = FALSE,
  doParallel  = TRUE,
  workers     = 4,
  return      = TRUE,
  file_name   = "Riaz"
)

# Keep clinical data in the same sample order as the deconvolution tables
traitData_train <- coldata_gide[rownames(deconv_train), , drop = FALSE]
traitData_test  <- coldata_riaz[rownames(deconv_test), , drop = FALSE]

saveRDS(list(deconv_train = deconv_train, deconv_test = deconv_test,
             traitData_train = traitData_train, traitData_test = traitData_test),
        file.path(results_dir, "deconvolution_tables.rds"))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Train classification model with leakage-free cross-validation
##    (deconvolution subgroups rebuilt inside every CV fold, via multideconv::prepare_multideconv_folds)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

res <- pipeML::compute_features.training.ML(
  features_train = deconv_train,
  target_var      = traitData_train$Response,
  task_type        = "classification",
  trait.positive   = "R",
  metric           = "AUROC",
  k_folds          = 5,
  n_rep            = 10,
  ncores           = NULL,
  return           = TRUE,
  file_name        = "Gide_training",
  fold_construction_fun       = multideconv::prepare_multideconv_folds,
  fold_construction_args_fixed = list(ncores = 4)
)

saveRDS(res, file.path(results_dir, "training_result.rds"))

cat("\n==== Cross-validation performance (Gide, training cohort) ====\n")
print(res$AUROC_median)
print(res$AUPRC_median)
cat("\nSelected model: ", res$Model$method, "\n")

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Predict on the independent Riaz cohort
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Project Riaz samples onto the deconvolution subgroups learned on Gide only
dt_test <- multideconv::replicate_deconvolution_subgroups(
  deconv_res         = res$Custom_output,
  deconvolution_test = deconv_test
)

pred <- pipeML::compute_prediction(
  model       = res$Model,
  test_data   = dt_test,
  target_var  = traitData_test$Response,
  task_type   = "classification",
  trait.positive = "R",
  file.name   = "Gide_to_Riaz",
  return      = TRUE
)

saveRDS(pred, file.path(results_dir, "test_prediction.rds"))

cat("\n==== Performance on the independent Riaz cohort ====\n")
print(pred$AUC)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. SHAP values: which TME subgroups drive the prediction?
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

shap <- pipeML::compute_shap_values(
  model_trained = res$Model,
  task_type     = "classification",
  seed          = 123
)

subgroup_composition <- res$Custom_output[["Deconvolution subgroups composition"]]

composition_txt <- file.path(results_dir, "top_feature_composition.txt")
sink(composition_txt)
for (feat in top_features) {
  cell_type <- NULL
  for (ct in names(subgroup_composition)) {
    if (feat %in% names(subgroup_composition[[ct]])) {
      cell_type <- ct
      break
    }
  }
  cat("Feature: ", feat, "\n", sep = "")
  if (!is.null(cell_type)) {
    cat("  Cell type: ", cell_type, "\n", sep = "")
    cat("  Composed of (method_signature estimates merged into this subgroup):\n")
    cat("   - ", paste(subgroup_composition[[cell_type]][[feat]], collapse = "\n   - "), "\n\n", sep = "")
  } else {
    cat("  (single feature, not part of a merged subgroup)\n\n")
  }
}
sink()

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 6. SHAP plots
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(shapviz))

X_shap <- res$Model$trainingData[rownames(shap), colnames(shap)]
sv <- shapviz::shapviz(as.matrix(shap), X = X_shap, baseline = attr(shap, "baseline"))

pdf(file.path(results_dir, "SHAP_importance_bar.pdf"), width = 7, height = 6)
print(shapviz::sv_importance(sv, kind = "bar") + ggplot2::ggtitle("Global feature importance (mean |SHAP|)"))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

summary_txt <- file.path(results_dir, "RESULTS_SUMMARY.txt")
sink(summary_txt)

cat("======================================================\n\n")
cat("Training cohort: Gide et al. (n = ", ncol(gide_tpm), "; R = ", sum(traitData_train$Response == "R"),
    ", NR = ", sum(traitData_train$Response == "NR"), ")\n", sep = "")
cat("Test cohort:     Riaz et al. (n = ", ncol(riaz_tpm), "; R = ", sum(traitData_test$Response == "R"),
    ", NR = ", sum(traitData_test$Response == "NR"), ")\n\n", sep = "")

cat("Deconvolution methods: ", paste(deconv_methods, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Number of raw deconvolution features (Gide): ", ncol(deconv_train), "\n")

cat("Best hyperparameters:\n")

tool_use_result.originalFile:
## TME composition -> immunotherapy response prediction
## Train on Gide et al. cohort, validate on Riaz et al. cohort (independent cohorts)
## Pipeline: multideconv (cell-type deconvolution + leakage-free subgroup folds) + pipeML (ML training/prediction/SHAP)

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(multideconv)
  library(pipeML)
  library(dplyr)
})

work_dir    <- "/home/marcelo.hurtado/Documents/tme_analysis/d91d50f6b3/work"
data_dir    <- file.path(work_dir, "data")
results_dir <- file.path(work_dir, "results")

setwd(results_dir)  # package functions write to "Results/" relative to the working directory

set.seed(123)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 1. Load data
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

coldata <- read.table(file.path(data_dir, "colData_all.txt"), header = TRUE, sep = " ", quote = "\"")
rownames(coldata) <- coldata$rna_id

gide <- read.delim(file.path(data_dir, "Gide_log2TPM.txt"), check.names = FALSE, row.names = 1)
riaz <- read.delim(file.path(data_dir, "Riaz_log2TPM.txt"), check.names = FALSE, row.names = 1)

# Values are log2(TPM + 1); multideconv expects linear-scale (TPM) counts
gide_tpm <- 2^gide - 1
riaz_tpm <- 2^riaz - 1
gide_tpm[gide_tpm < 0] <- 0
riaz_tpm[riaz_tpm < 0] <- 0

coldata_gide <- coldata[coldata$Cohort == "Gide", ]
coldata_riaz <- coldata[coldata$Cohort == "Riaz", ]

coldata_gide <- coldata_gide[colnames(gide_tpm), ]
coldata_riaz <- coldata_riaz[colnames(riaz_tpm), ]

stopifnot(all(rownames(coldata_gide) == colnames(gide_tpm)))
stopifnot(all(rownames(coldata_riaz) == colnames(riaz_tpm)))

cat("Gide (training cohort): ", ncol(gide_tpm), " samples - Response: ", paste(names(table(coldata_gide$Response)), table(coldata_gide$Response), sep = "=", collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Riaz (test cohort): ", ncol(riaz_tpm), " samples - Response: ", paste(names(table(coldata_riaz$Response)), table(coldata_riaz$Response), sep = "=", collapse = ", "), "\n")

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 2. Cell type deconvolution (first-generation methods, multideconv)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

deconv_methods <- c("Quantiseq", "Epidish", "DeconRNASeq", "DWLS")

deconv_train <- multideconv::compute.deconvolution(
  raw.counts  = gide_tpm,
  methods     = deconv_methods,
  normalized  = FALSE,   # input is already TPM-normalized (not raw counts)
  doParallel  = TRUE,
  workers     = 4,
  return      = TRUE,
  file_name   = "Gide"
)

deconv_test <- multideconv::compute.deconvolution(
  raw.counts  = riaz_tpm,
  methods     = deconv_methods,
  normalized  = FALSE,
  doParallel  = TRUE,
  workers     = 4,
  return      = TRUE,
  file_name   = "Riaz"
)

# compute.deconvolution() sanitizes sample names via data.frame() (e.g. digit-leading
# Gide IDs like "10_PD1_PRE" become "X10_PD1_PRE"); match clinical data on make.names()
rownames(coldata_gide) <- make.names(rownames(coldata_gide))
rownames(coldata_riaz) <- make.names(rownames(coldata_riaz))

# Keep clinical data in the same sample order as the deconvolution tables
traitData_train <- coldata_gide[rownames(deconv_train), , drop = FALSE]
traitData_test  <- coldata_riaz[rownames(deconv_test), , drop = FALSE]

saveRDS(list(deconv_train = deconv_train, deconv_test = deconv_test,
             traitData_train = traitData_train, traitData_test = traitData_test),
        file.path(results_dir, "deconvolution_tables.rds"))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 3. Train classification model with leakage-free cross-validation
##    (deconvolution subgroups rebuilt inside every CV fold, via multideconv::prepare_multideconv_folds)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

res <- pipeML::compute_features.training.ML(
  features_train = deconv_train,
  target_var      = traitData_train$Response,
  task_type        = "classification",
  trait.positive   = "R",
  metric           = "AUROC",
  k_folds          = 5,
  n_rep            = 10,
  ncores           = NULL,
  return           = TRUE,
  file_name        = "Gide_training",
  fold_construction_fun       = multideconv::prepare_multideconv_folds,
  fold_construction_args_fixed = list(ncores = 4)
)

saveRDS(res, file.path(results_dir, "training_result.rds"))

cat("\n==== Cross-validation performance (Gide, training cohort) ====\n")
print(res$AUROC_median)
print(res$AUPRC_median)
cat("\nSelected model: ", res$Model$method, "\n")

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 4. Predict on the independent Riaz cohort
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Project Riaz samples onto the deconvolution subgroups learned on Gide only
dt_test <- multideconv::replicate_deconvolution_subgroups(
  deconv_res         = res$Custom_output,
  deconvolution_test = deconv_test
)

pred <- pipeML::compute_prediction(
  model       = res$Model,
  test_data   = dt_test,
  target_var  = traitData_test$Response,
  task_type   = "classification",
  trait.positive = "R",
  file.name   = "Gide_to_Riaz",
  return      = TRUE
)

saveRDS(pred, file.path(results_dir, "test_prediction.rds"))

cat("\n==== Performance on the independent Riaz cohort ====\n")
print(pred$AUC)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 5. SHAP values: which TME subgroups drive the prediction?
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

shap <- pipeML::compute_shap_values(
  model_trained = res$Model,
  task_type     = "classification",
  seed          = 123
)

saveRDS(shap, file.path(results_dir, "shap_values.rds"))

importance <- sort(colMeans(abs(shap)), decreasing = TRUE)
importance_df <- data.frame(Feature = names(importance), Mean_abs_SHAP = unname(importance))
write.csv(importance_df, file.path(results_dir, "shap_feature_importance.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

cat("\n==== Top features driving the prediction (mean |SHAP|) ====\n")
print(head(importance_df, 15))

# Composition of the top subgroups (which method-signature-cell type estimates were merged)
subgroup_composition <- res$Custom_output[["Deconvolution subgroups composition"]]
top_features <- head(importance_df$Feature, 10)
composition_txt <- file.path(results_dir, "top_feature_composition.txt")
sink(composition_txt)
for (feat in top_features) {
  cell_type <- NULL
  for (ct in names(subgroup_composition)) {
    if (feat %in% names(subgroup_composition[[ct]])) {
      cell_type <- ct
      break
    }
  }
  cat("Feature: ", feat, "\n", sep = "")
  if (!is.null(cell_type)) {
    cat("  Cell type: ", cell_type, "\n", sep = "")
    cat("  Composed of (method_signature estimates merged into this subgroup):\n")
    cat("   - ", paste(subgroup_composition[[cell_type]][[feat]], collapse = "\n   - "), "\n\n", sep = "")
  } else {
    cat("  (single feature, not part of a merged subgroup)\n\n")
  }
}
sink()

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 6. SHAP plots
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

suppressPackageStartupMessages(library(shapviz))

X_shap <- res$Model$trainingData[rownames(shap), colnames(shap)]
sv <- shapviz::shapviz(as.matrix(shap), X = X_shap, baseline = attr(shap, "baseline"))

pdf(file.path(results_dir, "SHAP_importance_bar.pdf"), width = 7, height = 6)
print(shapviz::sv_importance(sv, kind = "bar") + ggplot2::ggtitle("Global feature importance (mean |SHAP|)"))
dev.off()

pdf(file.path(results_dir, "SHAP_beeswarm.pdf"), width = 7, height = 6)
print(shapviz::sv_importance(sv, kind = "beeswarm") + ggplot2::ggtitle("SHAP values across training samples"))
dev.off()

top_feature <- importance_df$Feature[1]
pdf(file.path(results_dir, "SHAP_dependence_top_feature.pdf"), width = 6, height = 5)
print(shapviz::sv_dependence(sv, v = top_feature))
dev.off()

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## 7. Written summary
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

summary_txt <- file.path(results_dir, "RESULTS_SUMMARY.txt")
sink(summary_txt)
cat("TME composition -> immunotherapy response prediction\n")
cat("======================================================\n\n")
cat("Training cohort: Gide et al. (n = ", ncol(gide_tpm), "; R = ", sum(traitData_train$Response == "R"),
    ", NR = ", sum(traitData_train$Response == "NR"), ")\n", sep = "")
cat("Test cohort:     Riaz et al. (n = ", ncol(riaz_tpm), "; R = ", sum(traitData_test$Response == "R"),
    ", NR = ", sum(traitData_test$Response == "NR"), ")\n\n", sep = "")

cat("Deconvolution methods: ", paste(deconv_methods, collapse = ", "), "\n")
cat("Number of raw deconvolution features (Gide): ", ncol(deconv_train), "\n")
cat("Number of deconvolution subgroup features used by the final model: ", ncol(res$Model$trainingData) - 1, "\n\n")

cat("Selected ML algorithm: ", res$Model$method, "\n")
cat("Best hyperparameters:\n")
print(res$Model$bestTune)

cat("\nCross-validation performance on Gide (median [MAD] across resamples):\n")
print(res$AUROC_median)
print(res$AUPRC_median)

cat("\nIndependent validation on Riaz:\n")
cat("  AUROC = ", round(pred$AUC$AUROC$estimate, 3),
    " [", round(pred$AUC$AUROC$lower, 3), "-", round(pred$AUC$AUROC$upper, 3), "]\n", sep = "")
cat("  AUPRC = ", round(pred$AUC$AUPRC$estimate, 3),
    " [", round(pred$AUC$AUPRC$lower, 3), "-", round(pred$AUC$AUPRC$upper, 3), "]\n", sep = "")

cat("\nTop features driving the prediction (mean |SHAP| on the training data):\n")
print(head(importance_df, 15))
sink()

cat("\n\nDone. Results saved in: ", results_dir, "\n")

content.text:
## Summary

**Approach:** trained on Gide et al. (n=73, 46R/27NR), validated on the independent Riaz et al. cohort (n=51, 10R/41NR) — a cross-cohort generalization test, not just a random split.

**Pipeline** (`scripts/run_analysis.R`):
1. Converted log2(TPM+1) → TPM, matched samples to `colData_all.txt` via `rna_id`.
2. `multideconv::compute.deconvolution()` — 4 methods (quanTIseq, EpiDISH, DeconRNASeq, DWLS) × 6 signatures → 284 raw deconvolution features per cohort.
3. `pipeML::compute_features.training.ML()` with `fold_construction_fun = multideconv::prepare_multideconv_folds` — rebuilds the deconvolution subgroups inside every one of 50 CV folds (5-fold × 10 repeats) so correlation structure from held-out samples never leaks into training. Random Forest was selected (CV AUROC 0.778, AUPRC 0.873 on Gide).
4. `multideconv::replicate_deconvolution_subgroups()` projected Riaz onto the subgroups learned on Gide; `pipeML::compute_prediction()` evaluated the final model.
5. `pipeML::compute_shap_values()` + `shapviz` for interpretability.

**Result:** on the independent Riaz cohort, AUROC = 0.63 [0.45–0.80], AUPRC = 0.26 [0.17–0.54] — modest but above chance, indicating the TME-composition signal generalizes only partially across these two cohorts (expected, given how different the two cohorts' response rates are: 63% vs 20%).

**Top features driving the prediction** (mean |SHAP|, in `shap_feature_importance.csv` and `top_feature_composition.txt`):
1. **Monocytes** (DeconRNASeq/TIL10)
2. **Macrophages M1** — consistent across DWLS/EpiDISH and DeconRNASeq/quanTIseq (two independent subgroups)
3. **CD8+ T cells** — a robust consensus subgroup built from 4 independent method/signature estimates
4. **Mast (resting) cells**, **Cancer cell fraction**, **B memory cells**, **NK (resting) cells**, **Macrophages M2**

Higher monocyte/M1-macrophage and CD8+ T cell estimates pushed predictions toward response, consistent with known anti-PD1 biology (inflamed, CD8-infiltrated tumors respond better).

All results (deconvolution matrices, CV plots, ROC/PR curves, SHAP plots/values, and `RESULTS_SUMMARY.txt`) are saved in `results/`.

content.text:
**1. Input data transformation**
Both `Gide_log2TPM.txt` and `Riaz_log2TPM.txt` were log2(TPM+1). I converted them back to linear TPM (`2^x - 1`, clipped at 0) before deconvolution, since `multideconv::compute.deconvolution()` expects linear-scale TPM/counts, not log-transformed values. I then called it with `normalized = FALSE` (meaning "already-normalized/TPM" input — the flag's naming is counterintuitive: `TRUE` means "raw counts, please TPM-normalize internally"). No other transformation was applied — deconvolution subgroup features, SHAP, and model inputs all operate on the (correctly-scaled) deconvolution output, not on raw expression.

**2. Methods run / skipped**
Ran: `compute.deconvolution()` with quanTIseq, EpiDISH, DeconRNASeq, DWLS (×6 signatures) on Gide and Riaz separately; `pipeML::compute_features.training.ML()` with `fold_construction_fun = multideconv::prepare_multideconv_folds` (11 classification algorithms tuned, RF selected); `replicate_deconvolution_subgroups()` to project Riaz onto Gide-learned subgroups; `compute_prediction()`; `compute_shap_values()` + `shapviz`.

Skipped: **CIBERSORTx (CBSX)** — requires credentials I wasn't given, so I excluded it from `methods`. **MOMF** and all second-generation (single-cell-based) deconvolution methods (AutoGeneS, BayesPrism, Bisque, CPM, MuSiC, SCDC) — these require an scRNA-seq reference, which wasn't provided in `data/`. **Batch correction** (`batch=` argument in `compute.deconvolution.analysis`) — not applicable since I deconvolved and trained/tested on separate cohorts rather than a pooled matrix.

**3. Non-default parameters**
- `normalized = FALSE` in `compute.deconvolution()` (default `TRUE`) — required given linear-TPM input, as above.
- `methods = c("Quantiseq","Epidish","DeconRNASeq","DWLS")` instead of default (which includes `CBSX`) — no credentials available.
- `doParallel = TRUE, workers = 4` — default is sequential; parallelized DWLS for speed given 20 cores available (kept conservative given ~4.6GB free RAM observed).
- `n_rep = 10` (vignette-suggested value) instead of the package default of `5` — more repeats for stabler CV estimates given a small training cohort (n=73).
- `k_folds = 5` is actually the pipeML default's companion value used in the tutorial (package default is `10`); I used 5 because with only 27 NR samples in Gide, 10-fold CV would leave very few NR samples per test fold.
- `fold_construction_args_fixed = list(ncores = 4)` — controls the internal parallel pool for `prepare_multideconv_folds`'s 50 folds; kept modest for the same memory-headroom reason.
- Everything else (`corr=0.7`, `zero_thr`, `cv_thr`, `metric="AUROC"`, `seed=123`, `preprocess=TRUE`) was left at package defaults.

**4. Problems encountered**
- **Sample-ID mismatch**: `compute.deconvolution()` calls `data.frame()` internally, which sanitizes column names via R's `make.names()` — Gide's digit-leading sample IDs (e.g. `10_PD1_PRE`) got silently prefixed to `X10_PD1_PRE` in the deconvolution output, while `colData_all.txt`'s `rna_id` stayed unprefixed. I caught this by inspecting a small test run's output rownames before the full run, and fixed it by applying `make.names()` to the clinical-data rownames before matching them to the deconvolution output, with `stopifnot()` checks confirming exact alignment and no `NA` responses afterward.
- **Runtime**: no outright errors, but DWLS deconvolution was the clear bottleneck (~74s for 5 samples × 4 methods in a timed test). I used this to estimate total runtime (~30 min for both cohorts) before committing to the full background run, rather than running blind.
- No other crashes, warnings-as-errors, or silent empty outputs were encountered; the `pca(... more components than matrix columns requested)` warnings from DeconRNASeq's internal PCA step are a routine informational warning from that package for samples with few informative genes, not a pipeline fault.

**5. Checks performed before trusting results**
- Verified `rna_id` in `colData_all.txt` matched expression-matrix column names 1:1 for both cohorts (73/73 Gide, 51/51 Riaz) before running anything.
- Verified no duplicated gene symbols in either expression file.
- Checked the value range of the input matrices (max ~13, consistent with log2(TPM+1), confirming the back-transformation was necessary and correctly scaled).
- Re-confirmed sample alignment after deconvolution via `stopifnot(rownames(traitData) == rownames(deconv))` and `!anyNA(Response)`.
- Inspected the CV leaderboard (`AUROC_median`/`AUPRC_median` across all 11 algorithms) rather than trusting only the top model, to see that RF/XGBoost were close and clearly ahead of weaker learners (sanity check that selection wasn't a fluke of one algorithm).
- Rendered and visually inspected the SHAP bar plot PDF to confirm it was generated correctly, not just that the file existed.
- Looked up the composition of the top SHAP features (`top_feature_composition.txt`) to confirm they correspond to biologically coherent, often multi-method consensus cell-type estimates (e.g. CD8 T cells agreed on by 4 independent method/signature combinations) rather than single noisy features.

**6. Limits / caveats**
- **Test-set performance is modest and imprecise**: AUROC 0.63 [0.45–0.80] on Riaz — the confidence interval crosses 0.5, so I can't claim reliable discrimination on this specific external cohort with n=51.
- **Severe class imbalance in the test cohort** (10 R vs 41 NR) inflates AUPRC interpretation difficulty and widens bootstrap CIs.
- **SHAP values describe the training (Gide) model's internal behavior**, not necessarily what generalizes to Riaz — I flagged in the script's logic (per package docs) that these should be read as "how the model uses features on training data," and the gap between CV AUROC (0.78) and external AUROC (0.63) suggests some overfitting to Gide-specific structure.
- **No CIBERSORTx or single-cell-based (2nd-generation) deconvolution** was included, so the TME feature space is limited to first-generation, signature-based methods only — results could differ with those added.
- **Only two cohorts available**; this is a single train/test split, not a multi-cohort LODO validation, so "generalization" here reflects one specific cohort pair, not a general property of the model.
- I did not attempt any biological-pathway interpretation or literature cross-validation of the top features beyond noting they're directionally consistent with known anti-PD1 immunobiology — this is a plausibility check, not independent confirmation.

One last step. Save copies of the results you already produced in a standard format, so that they can be compared with other analyses. Do not compute anything new, do not rerun any method and do not change any existing file: only convert what already exists. Put the files in results/standard/. If you did not produce an item, skip it and say so. If you produced several variants, export the one you presented as your main result. Tables are CSV files with one row per patient and a first column named `patient` holding the sample names exactly as in the input data.

- deconvolution_raw_Gide.csv and deconvolution_raw_Riaz.csv: the deconvolution matrix of each cohort as returned by the deconvolution step (all method, signature and cell-type features), before any harmonization.
- subgroups_composition.csv: the composition of the deconvolution subgroups that are features of the final model (the "Deconvolution subgroups composition" of the deconvolution analysis done on the training samples), one row per member, with columns subgroup and feature, where subgroup is the name used as a model feature and feature is the name of a raw deconvolution feature (not one row per patient).
- cv_performance.csv: one row per algorithm compared, with columns algorithm and cv_auroc (not one row per patient).
- test_predictions.csv: columns patient and probability_R: the predicted probability of response for each patient of the external test cohort.
- feature_importance.csv: one row per feature, with columns feature, cell_type and importance (for example mean absolute SHAP value), not one row per patient.
- shap_values.csv: SHAP values, one row per patient and one column per feature, if you computed them.
- info.json: {"selected_algorithm": ..., "training_cohort": ..., "test_cohort": ..., "features_built_inside_cv_folds": true or false, "cv_folds": ..., "cv_repeats": ..., "metric": ..., "cibersortx": true or false}.

## Convert already-produced results into standard, comparable CSV/JSON files.
## Reads only existing saved objects; computes nothing new, reruns no method.

suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(multideconv)
  library(jsonlite)
})

results_dir  <- "/home/marcelo.hurtado/Documents/tme_analysis/d91d50f6b3/work/results"
out_dir      <- file.path(results_dir, "standard")
dir.create(out_dir, showWarnings = FALSE)

# De-sanitize sample names mangled by data.frame()'s make.names() inside compute.deconvolution()
# (digit-leading Gide IDs got an "X" prefix; verified this recovers the exact original input names)
restore_names <- function(x) sub("^X([0-9])", "\\1", x)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## deconvolution_raw_Gide.csv / deconvolution_raw_Riaz.csv
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

dt <- readRDS(file.path(results_dir, "deconvolution_tables.rds"))

write_raw <- function(mat, file) {
  df <- data.frame(patient = restore_names(rownames(mat)), mat, check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
  write.csv(df, file, row.names = FALSE)
}

write_raw(dt$deconv_train, file.path(out_dir, "deconvolution_raw_Gide.csv"))
write_raw(dt$deconv_test,  file.path(out_dir, "deconvolution_raw_Riaz.csv"))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## subgroups_composition.csv
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

res <- readRDS(file.path(results_dir, "training_result.rds"))
final_features <- setdiff(colnames(res$Model$trainingData), ".outcome")

comp <- res$Custom_output[["Deconvolution subgroups composition"]]

rows <- list()
for (cell_type in names(comp)) {
  for (subgroup in names(comp[[cell_type]])) {
    if (subgroup %in% final_features) {
      members <- comp[[cell_type]][[subgroup]]
      rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(subgroup = subgroup, feature = members, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }
  }
}
subgroups_composition <- do.call(rbind, rows)
write.csv(subgroups_composition, file.path(out_dir, "subgroups_composition.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## cv_performance.csv  (metric used for model selection: AUROC)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

cv_perf <- data.frame(
  algorithm = res$AUROC_median$model,
  cv_auroc  = res$AUROC_median$Median_AUROC
)
write.csv(cv_perf, file.path(out_dir, "cv_performance.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## test_predictions.csv
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

pred <- readRDS(file.path(results_dir, "test_prediction.rds"))
test_predictions <- data.frame(
  patient         = restore_names(rownames(pred$Predictions)),
  probability_R   = pred$Predictions$yes
)
write.csv(test_predictions, file.path(out_dir, "test_predictions.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## feature_importance.csv  (feature, cell_type, importance = mean |SHAP|)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

importance_df <- read.csv(file.path(results_dir, "shap_feature_importance.csv"), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)

# cell_type of merged subgroup features: from the composition list keys
subgroup_to_celltype <- character(0)
for (cell_type in names(comp)) {
  for (subgroup in names(comp[[cell_type]])) {
    subgroup_to_celltype[subgroup] <- cell_type
  }
}

# cell_type of singleton (pass-through) raw features: longest matching suffix
# in multideconv's own cell type nomenclature (static package metadata)
nomenclature <- multideconv::get_cell_type_nomenclature()
nomenclature <- nomenclature[order(-nchar(nomenclature))]

match_celltype_suffix <- function(feature) {
  for (ct in nomenclature) {
    if (endsWith(feature, paste0("_", ct))) return(ct)
  }
  NA_character_
}

cell_type <- sapply(importance_df$Feature, function(f) {
  if (!is.na(subgroup_to_celltype[f])) return(unname(subgroup_to_celltype[f]))
  match_celltype_suffix(f)
})

feature_importance <- data.frame(
  feature    = importance_df$Feature,
  cell_type  = unname(cell_type),
  importance = importance_df$Mean_abs_SHAP
)
write.csv(feature_importance, file.path(out_dir, "feature_importance.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## shap_values.csv  (one row per training-cohort patient, one column per feature)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

shap <- readRDS(file.path(results_dir, "shap_values.rds"))
shap_out <- data.frame(patient = restore_names(rownames(shap)), as.data.frame(shap), check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL)
write.csv(shap_out, file.path(out_dir, "shap_values.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## info.json
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

info <- list(
  selected_algorithm = res$Model$method,
  training_cohort = "Gide",
  test_cohort = "Riaz",
  features_built_inside_cv_folds = TRUE,
  cv_folds = 5,
  cv_repeats = 10,
  metric = "AUROC",
  cibersortx = FALSE
)
writeLines(jsonlite::toJSON(info, auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE), file.path(out_dir, "info.json"))

cat("Done.\n")
cat(paste(list.files(out_dir), collapse = "\n"), "\n")

}

write_raw(dt$deconv_train, file.path(out_dir, "deconvolution_raw_Gide.csv"))
write_raw(dt$deconv_test,  file.path(out_dir, "deconvolution_raw_Riaz.csv"))

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
## subgroups_composition.csv
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

res <- readRDS(file.path(results_dir, "training_result.rds"))
final_features <- setdiff(colnames(res$Model$trainingData), ".outcome")

comp <- res$Custom_output[["Deconvolution subgroups composition"]]

rows <- list()
for (cell_type in names(comp)) {
  for (subgroup in names(comp[[cell_type]])) {
    if (subgroup %in% final_features) {
      members <- comp[[cell_type]][[subgroup]]
      rows[[length(rows) + 1]] <- data.frame(subgroup = subgroup, feature = members, stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
    }
  }
}
subgroups_composition <- do.call(rbind, rows)
write.csv(subgroups_composition, file.path(out_dir, "subgroups_composition.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## cv_performance.csv  (metric used for model selection: AUROC)
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  algorithm = res$AUROC_median$model,
  cv_auroc  = res$AUROC_median$Median_AUROC
)
write.csv(cv_perf, file.path(out_dir, "cv_performance.csv"), row.names = FALSE)

## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

)

for (cell_type in names(comp)) {
  for (subgroup in names(comp[[cell_type]])) {
    subgroup_to_celltype[subgroup] <- cell_type
  }
}

# in multideconv's own cell type nomenclature (static package metadata)
nomenclature <- multideconv::get_cell_type_nomenclature()
nomenclature <- nomenclature[order(-nchar(nomenclature))]

match_celltype_suffix <- function(feature) {
  for (ct in nomenclature) {
    if (endsWith(feature, paste0("_", ct))) return(ct)
  }
  NA_character_
}

cell_type <- sapply(importance_df$Feature, function(f) {
  if (!is.na(subgroup_to_celltype[f])) return(unname(subgroup_to_celltype[f]))
  match_celltype_suffix(f)
})

feature_importance <- data.frame(
  feature    = importance_df$Feature,
  cell_type  = unname(cell_type),
  importance = importance_df$Mean_abs_SHAP
)

## info.json
## ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

  training_cohort = "Gide",

  cv_folds = 5,

)
writeLines(jsonlite::toJSON(info, auto_unbox = TRUE, pretty = TRUE), file.path(out_dir, "info.json"))

cat("Done.\n")
cat(paste(list.files(out_dir), collapse = "\n"), "\n")
